terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the shop's folder, then go into shop and work there with git.

tasks.title: Ignore the till's stock export
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder, then work inside `shop`. Every evening the shop's till writes `stock.csv` into `shop`. It is not part of the website, and Git should leave it alone.

Open `shop/.gitignore` in the editor, write a pattern on its own line that matches `stock.csv`, and save. Do not stage or commit `stock.csv`.

The check asks Git whether a line of `shop/.gitignore` matches `stock.csv`, and expects `stock.csv` to be untracked and no page of the website to be ignored.
nextSteps: Run `git status` and find `stock.csv` under untracked files.
Open `shop/.gitignore` from the files panel. It is empty.
Write one line for the stock export and save the file.
Run `git status` again: `stock.csv` is no longer listed, and `.gitignore` is.
hints: Git reads the patterns from the file .gitignore in shop, one pattern per line.
The simplest pattern is the file's own name, spelled exactly as git status prints it.
Write the line `stock.csv` in .gitignore and save.

tasks.title: Ignore Femi's drafts folder
tasks.description:
Femi keeps pages he has not finished in the folder `drafts`, and he puts all kinds of files there. Add a line to `shop/.gitignore` that makes Git ignore the whole folder, whatever is in it now or later. Save the file.

The check asks Git about the files in `drafts` and about a file the check makes up inside it. Every one of them must be ignored, none tracked, and no page of the website ignored.
nextSteps: Run `git status`: it lists `drafts/` as one untracked folder.
Add one line to `.gitignore` for the folder and save.
Run `git status` again: `drafts/` is gone from the list.
hints: One line can take a whole folder, so you never list the files in it one by one.
A pattern that ends with a slash matches a folder and everything inside it.
Add the line `drafts/` to .gitignore and save.

tasks.title: Make Git forget upload.log, and keep the file
tasks.description:
Femi's upload tool writes `upload.log` every time he puts the site online, and a commit took it in by mistake. Since then `git status` lists it as modified after every upload.

Add a line for `upload.log` to `shop/.gitignore` and save. You will see that `git status` still lists it. Then take `upload.log` out of what Git tracks, while the file itself stays in `shop`, because the upload tool still writes to it.

The check expects a line of `.gitignore` to match `upload.log`, the file to be gone from the staging area, and the file to be still in the folder.
nextSteps: Add the line to `.gitignore`, save, and run `git status`: `upload.log` is still listed as modified.
Read the part of the lesson on files Git already tracks.
Take the file out of the staging area only, so it stays on disk.
Run `git status`: Git lists `upload.log` as deleted, to be committed, and the file is still in the files panel.
hints: A pattern in .gitignore only keeps out files Git does not track yet. upload.log is tracked, so Git has to be told to forget it.
`git rm` stops tracking a file, and on its own it deletes the file from the folder too. One option keeps the file on disk.

tasks.title: Commit .gitignore and the end of upload.log
tasks.description:
Save the new rules in the history: commit `.gitignore` together with the removal of `upload.log`, so whoever gets the shop's history next gets the same rules.

The check expects the first three tasks to be done, the last commit to hold `.gitignore` exactly as it is in the folder and no longer hold `upload.log`, `stock.csv` or the drafts, no other file of the website to be changed, and `git status` to have nothing left to commit.
nextSteps: Run `git status`: `.gitignore` is untracked and the deletion of `upload.log` is staged.
Commit with a message that says what Git leaves alone from now on.
Run `git status`: nothing to commit, working tree clean.
hints: .gitignore is a file like any other. Until it is committed, only this folder knows its patterns.
The removal of upload.log is already staged. Add .gitignore to the staging area and both go into one commit.
Run `git add .gitignore`, then `git commit -m "Ignore the stock export, the drafts and the upload log"`.
